messages.author: 21e2646f0cc9f243
messages.subject: Mesh construction
parts:
I'm trying to create a mesh over a specified region. However, inside the region, I have an area where data was not collected. Should I ignore the area and triangulate over the whole region, then remove the region after predicting? Below is the code which I am using to construct the mesh

```
nyeri <- county_shapefile |> 
  filter(county == "Nyeri")
st_crs(nyeri) <- NA

outer_boundaries <- county_shapefile |> 
  filter(county %in% c( all_hook$county)) |> 
  st_union() |> 
  st_sf() 

kenya_shp1 <- as(as(st_transform(outer_boundaries, epsgKM(32737)), 'Spatial'), 'SpatialPolygonsDataFrame')
coords_mesh = coords.schs
kenya_shp <- fortify(kenya_shp1)
bdry <- inla.sp2segment(kenya_shp1)
shp.bnd <- cbind(kenya_shp$long, kenya_shp$lat)
c.bnd <- as.matrix(shp.bnd)

mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(
  boundary = bdry,
  loc = coords_mesh,
  loc.domain = c.bnd,
  max.edge = c(20, 40),
  cutoff = 1
)
par(mfrow = c(1,2))
plot(bdry);plot(mesh)

```

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Mesh construction
parts:
Hi,
This really only matters if forcing the mesh triangle edges to conform to the inner region boundary makes the mesh needlessly complex.
What matters more is how you use the regions in the model; for point process models, you must specify the proper observation regions in the likelihood construction; this is separate from whether the mesh edges follow those regions or not.

Also, nowadays you shouldn’t need to convert to sp objects or sp2segment; the underlying fmesher functions accept sf polygons and do any potentially required conversions internally.


Finn
